thread.title: Jabil's new debt deal could mean millions in savings

author: Margie Manning
title: Jabil's new debt deal could mean millions in savings
text: – Finance Editor,   3:00pm EST Updated Jan 11, 2018, 3:20pm EST Jabil Inc. expects to save more than $15 million each year with a new debt offering. Moody’s Investors Service cites the annual savings in a Jan. 9 report that also projects a mostly positive future for Jabil (NYSE: JBL), a St. Petersburg-based electronic services firm and the second-largest publicly traded company in the Tampa Bay area, with $19.5 billion in revenue in the 12 months ended Nov. 30. Moody’s expects Jabil to continue to diversify its revenue base and generate more cash, supporting its position as a leader in its industry. Moody’s assigned a Ba1 rating, the highest non-investment grade rating Moody’s assigns, to Jabil’s offering of $500 million in senior unsecured notes. Jabil will use the proceeds to redeem about $400 million in notes issued earlier. S&P Global Ratings gave an investment grade rating to the notes, rating them BBB-. Both credit organizations cited concerns about high customer concentration. About 24 percent of Jabil’s revenue comes from Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL). Jabil makes casings for Apple’s iPhone. But Jabil has been expanding its footprint and using a broader mix of materials technologies along with higher complexity products and services, Moody’s said. “The company’s global scale and production capabilities have grown organically and through acquisitions over the past decade, providing the company with a platform to win customer orders around the world,” Moody’s said. Moody’s also assigned a positive outlook to the new debt offering, saying it believes Jabil’s future growth will be accomplished through internally generated business, with acquisition activity largely focused on augmenting its existing operations, and with low risk of a large acquisition in the near future.
